newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two months of winter killed 205 Mexicans - report.
newsitem.headline: Two months of winter killed 205 Mexicans - report.

text.p: Two months of unusually frigid winter weather have claimed 205 lives in Mexico, state-owned news agency Notimex reported on Thursday.

Notimex said the northern states of Chihuahua, Coahuila and Nuevo Leon were the hardest hit by the coldest December and January in three decades. In some cases, temperatures plummeted to minus 20 degrees Celsius (-4 degrees Fahrenheit).

In Chihuahua alone, 87 people died during the past two months and 32 people were killed in the past two weeks following a cold snap that brought several rare snowfalls but also bone-chilling temperatures, according to officials there.

"Most of the people have died of hypothermia, but we have also had many cases of people dying from inhaling carbon monoxide from their home heating units," Dr. Oscar Martin Nacif, head of the state's civil protection agency, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
